issues.description: The rule requires using Python 3.12+ modern type syntax (set[tuple[str, ...]] instead of Set[Tuple[str, ...]]), but the code imports and uses legacy typing module classes Set and Tuple

issues.title: Type mismatch in blocks_variable_output prevents variable blocking
issues.description: The blocks_variable_output method compares a Sequence (assigned_variable_selector) directly against a set of tuples (variable_selectors), but fails to convert the Sequence to a tuple first. This type mismatch causes the 'in' check to always return False, meaning the Variable Assigner node will never properly block streaming output of conversation variables. As a result, the response coordinator will incorrectly allow streaming to proceed before conversation variables are updated, violating the intended synchronization logic and potentially showing stale variable values to users.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
def blocks_variable_output(self, variable_selectors: Set[Tuple[str, ...]]) -> bool:
    """
    Check if this Variable Assigner node blocks the output of specific variables.

    Returns True if this node updates any of the requested conversation variables.
    """
    assigned_selector = self.node_data.assigned_variable_selector
    return assigned_selector in variable_selectors

issues.title: Incorrect input value used in NodeRunResult for CLEAR mode
issues.description: The code attempts to use updated_variable.to_object() for the CLEAR write mode's input value, but this represents the final cleared state rather than the input that triggered the operation. In CLEAR mode, income_value is actually the zero value generated by SegmentType.get_zero_value(), which is what should be shown as the input. This causes the NodeRunResult to misrepresent what value was used as input to the clear operation, breaking observability and potentially confusing downstream systems that rely on accurate input tracking.

issues.title: Test uses list equality instead of tuple conversion for event selector
issues.description: The test compares event.selector (which is a Sequence[str]) with a list literal using ==. While this might work in some cases due to Python's sequence equality, it's fragile and inconsistent with the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase. The original code correctly converted to tuple for comparison (tuple(event.selector) == ('conversation', 'conv_var')). This change breaks the filtering logic and will likely cause the test to fail to properly identify conversation variable chunk events, leading to false test failures.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
conv_var_chunk_events = [
    event
    for event in events
    if isinstance(event, NodeRunStreamChunkEvent) and event.selector == ["conversation", "conv_var"]
]

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30832 - fix(api): defer streaming response until referenced variables are updated

structured_output.summary:
The PR tries to stop Answer nodes from streaming before a v1 Variable Assigner has updated the conversation variable they read. The root cause is real: `VariableAssignerNode` v1 never overrides `blocks_variable_output`, so the response coordinator treats it as non-blocking. The PR adds an override that mirrors the existing v2 implementation, plus a CLEAR-mode `inputs.value` change, an end-to-end fixture, and a test.

The override has a crash bug. `assigned_variable_selector` is a `Sequence[str]` that pydantic stores as a `list`, and the override tests `list in set_of_tuples`. That raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` for every v1 assigner upstream of an Answer node, so the change breaks workflows that work today. The PR's own new test follows exactly that path (start → assigner → answer) and should fail on this head. I confirmed the type behavior with pydantic and traced the call path statically; I did not execute the test suite.
structured_output.verdictRationale: A critical runtime crash in the core change: any v1 Variable Assigner on a path to an Answer node raises during graph setup. The fix is a one-line tuple conversion, but it must land before merge. The unrelated CLEAR-mode change and the typing style nits can be cleaned up alongside it.

architecture.overview:
Dify's advanced-chat workflows stream Answer node text while upstream nodes are still running. The ResponseStreamCoordinator (`api/core/workflow/graph_engine/response_coordinator/coordinator.py`) builds, for each response node, a set of paths from the root and records which edges are blocking. An edge blocks when its source node is a branch, container, or response node, or when the source node's `blocks_variable_output(variable_selectors)` returns True. The variable selectors come from the Answer template's `VariableSegment`s. Base `Node.blocks_variable_output` returns False, so only nodes that override it can hold back streaming.

This PR adds the override to `VariableAssignerNode` v1, so an assigner that writes a conversation variable blocks any Answer that reads that variable until it finishes. The v2 assigner already did this. Separately, the CLEAR branch of v1 `_run` now reports the updated variable's value in `inputs.value`. The new override compares a list-typed selector against a set of tuples, which is where the crash comes from.
steps: Entry point: the graph engine registers each response (Answer) node with the coordinator. `register` calls `_build_paths_map`, which walks the graph from the root and computes the blocking edges for that node.

Inside `_build_paths_map`, the coordinator gathers the variable selectors from the Answer template and calls `blocks_variable_output` on every non-branch, non-container, non-response source node along each path.

The PR adds `VariableAssignerNode.blocks_variable_output` in `variable_assigner/v1/node.py` (lines 36-43). It returns True when the assigned conversation selector is among the requested selectors. The comparison is the bug: the assigned selector is a list, and the set holds tuples.
The `_run` change in the same file (lines 102-111) alters what v1 reports as `inputs.value` in CLEAR mode. This is not part of the streaming fix.

Tests: a new YAML fixture (start → assigner → answer, `over-write` to `conversation.conv_var`) and an end-to-end test that checks conversation-variable stream chunks match the query. There are no unit tests for the override itself.

findings.title: Override crashes on list-vs-set membership for every v1 assigner
findings.body:
The override compares `self.node_data.assigned_variable_selector` against a set of tuples. That value is a pydantic-validated `list`, so `list in set` raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'`. Python hashes the left operand before it checks the set, so this happens even when the set is empty.

The coordinator calls this method for every non-branch, non-container, non-response source node on every path to an Answer node (`coordinator.py:220`). The failure is therefore raised during graph setup, for any v1 assigner upstream of an Answer node. Before this PR the base class returned False, so these workflows ran normally. The fixture this PR adds (`start -> assigner -> answer`) follows exactly this path and should fail.

I confirmed the type behavior with pydantic v2: `Sequence[str]` yields a `list`, and `list in {('conversation','conv_var')}` raises `TypeError`. I did not run the test suite, but the path is deterministic.

::diff{file="api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py" lines="36-43"}

::suggestion{file="api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py" lines="42-43"}
assigned_selector = tuple(self.node_data.assigned_variable_selector)
return assigned_selector in variable_selectors
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py`, `VariableAssignerNode.blocks_variable_output` (lines 36-43) compares `self.node_data.assigned_variable_selector`, which pydantic stores as a list, against a set of tuples. That raises `TypeError: unhashable type 'list'`. Convert the selector to a tuple before the membership test. Match the `tuple(...)` normalization the coordinator uses in `api/core/workflow/graph_engine/response_coordinator/coordinator.py`. Then run `api/tests/unit_tests/core/workflow/graph_engine/test_streaming_conversation_variables.py` to confirm the v1 overwrite case passes.

findings.title: No unit tests for the new override's contract
findings.body:
The only new test is an end-to-end fixture run. The override's contract is small and deterministic, and it needs its own unit tests:

- A matching `('conversation', 'conv_var')` selector returns `True`.
- A non-matching selector returns `False`.
- An empty set returns `False`.

A test that builds the node from a real `VariableAssignerData`, where pydantic stores the selector as a list, would have exposed the `TypeError` above immediately. The end-to-end ordering assertion at line 75 is still useful: if the Answer streamed before the assignment, the chunks would show the old value. It only catches that if the workflow runs at all, and the current override stops the run first.

::code{file="api/tests/unit_tests/core/workflow/graph_engine/test_streaming_conversation_variables.py" lines="50-77"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/tests/unit_tests/core/workflow/graph_engine/`, add focused unit tests for `VariableAssignerNode.blocks_variable_output` in the v1 node. Cover three cases: a matching conversation selector returns True, a non-matching selector returns False, and an empty `variable_selectors` set returns False. Construct the node from a `VariableAssignerData` whose `assigned_variable_selector` is a list, as pydantic produces it, so the test would catch the unhashable-list bug. Follow the style of the existing tests in that directory.

findings.title: Unexplained inputs.value change for CLEAR mode
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py`, `_run` (around lines 102-111) now reports `updated_variable.to_object()` as `inputs.value` in CLEAR mode, while the other modes report `income_value.to_object()`. Either revert that change, or explain it in the PR and add a test that asserts `inputs.value` for CLEAR mode. Keep it out of the streaming fix, since it is not part of the root cause.

findings.title: Deprecated typing.Set/Tuple instead of builtin generics
findings.body:
The signature uses `Set[Tuple[str, ...]]` from `typing`. The base class (`nodes/base/node.py:435`) and the v2 override use `set[tuple[str, ...]]`. Use the builtin form for consistency.

::diff{file="api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py" lines="2-2"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py`, the import on line 2 brings in `Set` and `Tuple` from `typing`, and `blocks_variable_output` (line 36) uses them. Switch to the builtin lowercase `set[tuple[str, ...]]` annotation, the same style as the base class in `core/workflow/nodes/base/node.py` and the v2 override. Remove the now-unused typing imports.

findings.title: Root-cause fix mirrors the existing v2 pattern
findings.body: The root cause is real. The base `Node.blocks_variable_output` returns `False`, so the response coordinator can start streaming an Answer while a v1 assigner is still updating the conversation variable it reads. Giving v1 the same override that v2 already has, with the same docstring style, keeps the two versions consistent. The direction is right, and the defect is only in how the selector is compared, covered in the critical finding above.
